parts.label: A
parts.your_answer: The bottom template strand. Its 3' end is on the left, so the new strand runs 5' to 3' from left to right. That means it grows in the same direction the fork moves (rightward), so it can be made continuously.

parts.label: B
parts.your_answer: DNA polymerase can only add nucleotides to the 3' end of a growing strand. The new strand on the top template must grow 5' to 3' from right to left, which is away from the fork. So it is made in short pieces (Okazaki fragments). Each new piece starts with a new primer as more template is opened up. DNA ligase later joins the pieces.

parts.label: C
parts.your_answer: 3'-CTAGGAGCG-5' (the left end is 3' and the right end is 5').

parts.label: D
parts.your_answer: The new DNA molecule is the original top template strand paired with the newly made complementary strand. Each daughter molecule keeps one parent strand and has one new strand, and that is what semiconservative replication means.

parts.label: A
parts.your_answer: Water potential (Ψ) is the potential energy of water per unit volume relative to pure water, set by solute potential plus pressure potential (Ψ = Ψs + Ψp). It measures how strongly water tends to move. Water moves from higher (less negative) to lower (more negative) water potential.

parts.label: B
parts.your_answer: Put sucrose molarity (M) on the x-axis (the independent variable) and percent change in mass (%) on the y-axis (the dependent variable). Use evenly spaced scales and make the y-axis run from about -25 to +10 so the negative values fit. Plot all six points and connect them or draw a best-fit line. The points fall on a straight line with a negative slope.

parts.label: C
parts.your_answer: (i) The data fit a straight line, % change = 7 - 28 × M, which crosses 0% at about 0.25 M (between 0.2 and 0.4 M). (ii) Null hypothesis: sucrose molarity has no effect on the percent change in mass of the potato cores.

parts.label: D
parts.your_answer: The cores would lose more mass in 0.4 M NaCl than the -4.2% in 0.4 M sucrose. NaCl splits into two ions (i = 2), so the solution has about twice as many solute particles. Since Ψs = -iCRT, the solute potential, and so the water potential, of the NaCl solution is lower (more negative). More water therefore moves out of the cores by osmosis.

parts.label: A
parts.your_answer: A change in the DNA nucleotide sequence (a substitution, insertion or deletion) changes the mRNA codons transcribed from it. This can change the amino acid sequence of the protein: one amino acid may be swapped, a frameshift may change many amino acids, or a premature stop codon may cut the protein short. A different primary structure can change how the protein folds, and so its shape and function.

parts.label: B
parts.your_answer: Independent variable: how long the cells are exposed to UV light (0, 10, 20 or 30 s). Dependent variable: the number of colonies (antibiotic-resistant cells) that grow on the antibiotic plates.

parts.label: C
parts.your_answer: The longer the UV exposure, the more colonies will grow on the antibiotic plates. The 0 s plate should have the fewest colonies, possibly none.

parts.label: D
parts.your_answer: UV light damages DNA (for example, by forming thymine dimers), which leads to mutations when the DNA is repaired or copied. Longer exposure causes more DNA damage and more mutations, so more cells are likely to get a mutation that makes them resistant to the antibiotic. Because most cells survive, these resistant mutants can grow into colonies.

parts.label: A
parts.your_answer: The pesticide acts as a selective pressure. Insects with the resistance allele are more likely to survive and reproduce, so they pass the allele to more offspring. Over the generations, the allele's frequency rises.

parts.label: B
parts.your_answer: A line or scatter graph with Generation (0–12) on the x-axis and Frequency of the resistance allele (percent, 0–100) on the y-axis. The axes need labels, units and suitable scales, and all 7 points should be plotted and connected. The curve is S-shaped.

parts.label: C
parts.your_answer: (i) (57.6 − 7.6)/(6 − 2) = 50/4 = 12.5 percentage points per generation. (ii) Interpolating between generation 4 (25.1%) and generation 6 (57.6%), the frequency passes 50% at about generation 5.5. Any answer between 5 and 6 is acceptable.

parts.label: D
parts.your_answer: The frequency would go down. Without the pesticide, the allele lowers survival, so carriers have lower fitness and leave fewer offspring. Selection would then work against the allele.
